import { requireCustomer } from "./customers.js";
import { invoiceTotalCents } from "./invoices.js";

/** The invoices of one customer with their total, for the customer statement page. */
export function customerStatement(invoices, customers, customerId) {
  const customer = requireCustomer(customers, customerId);
  const own = invoices.filter((invoice) => invoice.customerId === customerId);

    customer,
    invoiceIds: own.map((invoice) => invoice.id),
    totalCents: own.reduce((sum, invoice) => sum + invoiceTotalCents(invoice), 0),

# invoice-export

Turns the invoices of the billing system into the CSV file the accounting team imports every month.

## Usage

```
npm run export > invoices.csv
```

This runs `node src/cli.js data`: it reads `invoices.json`, `billing-customers.json` and `crm-customers.json` from
the given directory (default `data/`) and prints one CSV row per invoice, in the order of `invoices.json`.

The customers come from two systems. `billing-customers.json` is exported by the billing system, and
`crm-customers.json` holds the customers that were created in the CRM. Both are read as they are delivered. The
accounting import expects the CSV columns `invoice_id,customer,issued_on,total`, so the format must not change.

## Tests

```
npm test
```

Plain `node --test`, no dependencies. Tests live in `tests/`.

## Conventions

- Money is handled in integer cents and formatted only at the edge (`src/money.js`).
- A reference to something that does not exist, such as an unknown customer, is a data error. It is reported with
  `UnknownReferenceError` naming what was not found (see `requireCustomer`), and the CLI then exits with status 1
  and prints nothing to stdout. The export never skips a record or prints a placeholder for it: a file with a
  missing invoice is worse for accounting than no file.

content.text:
The export now runs end to end and writes all 8 invoices, including INV-1041 (Birch & Co). The 12 tests pass.

**Cause:** the customers come from two systems that name the ID field differently. Billing uses `customerId`, but the CRM file uses `customer_id`. `buildCustomerIndex` only read `customerId`, so every CRM customer (C-2201, C-2202, C-2203) was indexed under `undefined`. Any invoice for one of them then found no customer and crashed. That's why only some invoices failed.

**Changes:**
- **`src/customers.js`:** `buildCustomerIndex` accepts either key and normalizes it to `customerId`. I left the input files alone, since the README says they're read as delivered.
- **`src/export.js`:** the export now looks customers up with `requireCustomer`. A genuinely unknown customer gives `Unknown customer "X" (referenced by invoice INV-…)` and exit status 1 with no output. That follows the README rule that the export never skips a record or prints a placeholder. Before, it was a bare `TypeError`.
- **`tests/customers.test.js`:** I added a test for CRM-style records. I also changed three existing assertions from `equal` to `deepEqual`, because the index now stores a normalized copy of each record.

Nothing is committed. Run `npm run export > invoices.csv` to produce the file for accounting.
